# Spec Quality Gate Checklist: Strategy Engine

**Purpose**: Formal-gate validation of requirements quality in `spec.md` — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and coverage across safety & signal integrity, backtest parity & determinism, failure & recovery flows, and contracts & integration — before `/speckit.plan`
**Created**: 2026-07-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Safety & Signal Integrity

- [x] CHK001 Are the validation rules that make a signal "invalid" enumerated exhaustively (confidence bounds, direction, required fields, expiry ordering), or could a strategy emit a structurally valid but semantically absurd signal (e.g., expiry years in the future) that no requirement rejects? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §SRC-003] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-008 now caps `expiry` at a configurable `max_expiry_window` (default 1 hour) after `timestamp`.
- [x] CHK002 Is "fail closed" defined identically everywhere it appears — do §FR-008 (reject, never coerce), §SRC-003 (drop, never repair), and the invalid-signal edge case agree on logging, counting, and alerting side effects? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §SRC-003] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-008 (reject/log/count/health state), SRC-003 (drop, never repair), FR-020 (validation-failure alerts), and the edge case all describe the same side effects; no contradiction.
- [x] CHK003 Is the boundary of SRC-002's "no I/O in strategies" precisely drawn — does it unambiguously forbid file reads (e.g., an ML strategy loading model weights), or only network/database/Redis access? [Ambiguity, Spec §SRC-002] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: the prohibition is an explicit enumeration (network I/O, database writes, direct Redis); local file access is not restricted, and parameters arrive via configuration (FR-002, FR-021). Artifact loading for ML strategies remains tracked under CHK004.
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for how an ML or model-backed strategy obtains its parameters/artifacts given the no-I/O constraint, or is that intentionally deferred and stated as out of scope? [Gap, Spec §SRC-002] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: new Assumption — artifacts load at instantiation from config-supplied paths, before event processing; runtime I/O stays prohibited; no ML strategy ships in this feature.
- [x] CHK005 Is the rate-limit behavior (§FR-017) reconciled with the decision-change emission rule (§FR-010) — can a legitimate strategy on a fast horizon ever hit 10 signals/asset/minute, and is the chosen default justified anywhere? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §FR-017] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-017 now justifies the default (FR-010 restricts emission to decision changes; sustained flapping above it indicates a defect) and notes the per-strategy override for fast horizons.
- [x] CHK006 Is it specified whether rate-limited (dropped) signals count as "emitted" for the §FR-010 re-emission rule and for the health check's last-signal-emitted observation? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017, §FR-019] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-010 now states only published signals count; validation/rate-limit drops increment per-strategy drop counters instead.
- [x] CHK007 Are the semantics of a HOLD signal defined for downstream interpretation — does HOLD mean "close positions", "abstain", or "explicitly neutral vote", and does the aggregator contract need this distinction? [Gap, Spec §FR-007, §FR-010] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-007 now defines HOLD as an explicit neutral vote, never "close positions"; position management is downstream.
- [x] CHK008 Is "bounded human-readable text" for `reasoning` quantified with an actual length limit, and is the bound's enforcement point (strategy vs engine validation) specified? [Clarity, Spec §SRC-006, §FR-008] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-007 sets a 500-character maximum, enforced by engine validation (FR-008), fail-closed like every other bound.
- [x] CHK009 Are staleness requirements complete for the sentiment input, or does §FR-014 only govern market-data staleness — can a strategy act on a week-old sentiment score with no requirement preventing it? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-014, §FR-016] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-014 now sets per-input thresholds — 60 s market data (= ingestion `gap_threshold`), 900 s sentiment (3× news poll interval).
- [x] CHK010 Is the interaction between staleness and already-published signals specified — when an asset's data goes stale, do previously published unexpired signals get retracted, or does expiry alone bound their lifetime? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-014, §SRC-003] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-014 now states staleness suppresses new signals only; published signals are bounded by `expiry` alone, no retraction mechanism.
- [x] CHK011 Can SRC-005 ("absence of a signal is always the safe default") be objectively verified given that downstream services are not yet specified — is the assumption that the aggregator treats silence as neutral documented? [Assumption, Measurability, Spec §SRC-005] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: new Assumption documents that the aggregator treats absent/expired signals as neutral.
- [x] CHK012 Are the PII/credential prohibitions (§SRC-006, SC-008) backed by a defined verification method (e.g., what counts as PII in log output), or is SC-008 unmeasurable as written? [Measurability, Spec §SRC-006, §SC-008] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: SC-008 now names the method — automated payload/log scans in tests, plus no-personal-data-inputs by construction.

## Backtest Parity & Determinism

- [x] CHK013 Is "identical signal sequence" defined precisely enough to test — does it include `timestamp` and `expiry` fields, and if so, is the requirement that they derive from event time (not wall clock) stated for the *emission* path, not just strategy logic? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, §SC-003] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-011 and SC-003 now state identity covers every field including `timestamp` and `expiry`, both event-time-derived.
- [x] CHK014 Does the determinism requirement address strategies with inherent randomness (ML inference, sampling) — is seeding required, or are nondeterministic strategies excluded from §FR-011's guarantee? [Gap, Spec §FR-011] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-011 imposes blanket determinism on every strategy (identical inputs + parameters → identical signals); a nondeterministic implementation is non-compliant by construction. Seeding is an implementation means, owned by the plan.
- [x] CHK015 Is the requirement that strategies cannot detect live-vs-backtest mode (§FR-012) reconciled with wall-clock-adjacent engine behaviors — health checks, rate limits (per minute of *what* time?), and reconnect backoff — is it specified which clock each engine subsystem uses? [Consistency, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012, §FR-017, §FR-019] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: everything strategy-observable is event-time (FR-011; FR-017 now explicit); health endpoint and reconnect backoff are operational wall-clock subsystems invisible to strategy logic (SRC-002, FR-012 boundary), so no parity leak.
- [x] CHK016 Is the rate limit (§FR-017) defined in event time or wall time, and is its effect on backtest replay at accelerated speed specified — would a 1-year replay at 1000× speed spuriously rate-limit correct signals? [Conflict, Spec §FR-017, §FR-011] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-017 now specifies an event-time rolling window (deterministic drops, replay-safe); sink burst absorption is explicitly assigned to the FR-012 sink seam, not the rate limit.
- [x] CHK017 Are the "source/sink seams" of §FR-012 defined as contract obligations this feature must deliver (what the replay source must provide, what the alternative sink must accept), or only as a deferred promise to nexus-backtest? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, §SBC-005] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-012 makes supporting the seams a MUST for this feature (not a deferred promise); the concrete seam interfaces are plan/contract artifacts per SBC-005.
- [x] CHK018 Is warm-up restart behavior after a gap (§FR-013) specified identically for live and replay contexts — does a replayed historical gap trigger the same warm-up restart, and is that the intended backtest semantics? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-011] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-013 is unconditional and FR-012 forbids mode branching, so gap→warm-up-restart is identical live and replayed by construction; that is the intended semantics.
- [x] CHK019 Is the deduplication/out-of-order behavior (§FR-015, edge cases) deterministic — given the same input sequence including duplicates and out-of-order events, is the "excluded from indicator computation" rule sufficient to guarantee identical strategy state? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015, §FR-011] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: the exclusion rule and duplicate handling are pure functions of the delivered sequence, so FR-011's guarantee (identical sequence incl. duplicates/out-of-order → identical state) holds.
- [x] CHK020 Does SC-003 specify the required fixture scope (event types, duplicates, gaps, out-of-order cases) for the determinism test, or could a trivially small fixture pass while real divergence risks go untested? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: SC-003 now requires the fixture to include a warm-up boundary, duplicates, out-of-order events, a data gap, and threshold crossings.
- [x] CHK021 Is "accelerated-speed replay" in SC-003 quantified (how fast, relative to what), and is the pass criterion identical-output rather than latency-based? [Clarity, Spec §SC-003] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: the pass criterion is output identity, which FR-011 makes speed-independent; any faster-than-real-time factor exercises the property, so quantifying the speed adds nothing.

## Failure & Recovery Flows

- [x] CHK022 Are the exponential backoff parameters (initial delay, multiplier, cap) and the default maximum restart attempts specified or explicitly delegated to configuration with defaults? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-005 now adopts nexus-ingestion's supervisor defaults — 1.0 s base doubling, 60 s cap, max 10 attempts (0 = unlimited).
- [x] CHK023 Is the state a restarted strategy resumes with defined — does it restart with empty indicator state (re-entering warm-up), and is that stated as a requirement rather than implied? [Gap, Spec §FR-005, §FR-013] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-024 now states it explicitly — a restarted strategy "re-enters warm-up with empty state (FR-005, FR-013)".
- [x] CHK024 Is the hang scenario (User Story 3, scenario 4) backed by a functional requirement — is there a per-strategy evaluation timeout or only the assertion that siblings are not delayed? [Gap, Spec §US3, §SRC-004] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-005 now defines a per-strategy evaluation timeout (default 5 s); a timed-out evaluation is treated as a crash under the same backoff.
- [x] CHK025 Are acknowledgment semantics specified for the multi-strategy fan-out — when is an input stream entry XACKed if three strategies consume it and one crashes mid-evaluation, and is signal-loss vs signal-duplication on crash recovery explicitly chosen? [Ambiguity, Gap, Spec §FR-001, §SBC-001] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: new FR-024 specifies ack-after-healthy-strategies-complete; strategy crash never blocks ack (at-least-once per process, best-effort per strategy, loss safe per SRC-005); duplicate tolerance added to SBC-002 and a crash-mid-evaluation edge case added.
- [x] CHK026 Are pending-message recovery requirements (claim/sweep of entries stuck pending after a crash, dead-letter handling) defined for this service's consumer groups, or intentionally omitted relative to the 002 precedent (FR-015 there)? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-001] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: new FR-025 adopts 002's mechanism — `XAUTOCLAIM` sweep every 60 s, 300 s claim threshold, dead-letter log + ack + `DEAD_LETTER_CLAIMED` alert.
- [x] CHK027 Is behavior specified for Redis loss on the *input* side (consumers) as opposed to the output publisher — reconnect expectations, health alerts, and whether strategies keep running on buffered state? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-022, §FR-020] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: new FR-025 — consumers reconnect with FR-005's backoff, emit `REDIS_DISCONNECT`; strategies need no degraded mode since their data turns stale (FR-014) and emission stops.
- [x] CHK028 Is the bounded signal buffer's overflow policy specified (drop-oldest vs drop-newest, alerting), and is its default size stated? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-022 now specifies 10,000 entries, drop-oldest — matching the platform `RedisPublisher` buffer in ingestion and sentiment.
- [x] CHK029 Is the shutdown timeout for in-flight evaluations quantified with a default, and is the fate of signals produced after the timeout expires specified? [Clarity, Spec Edge Cases (SIGTERM)] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: SIGTERM edge case now sets a 5 s default (the platform's shutdown-wait precedent); timed-out evaluations are cancelled, their signals never produced (safe per SRC-005).
- [x] CHK030 Are the recovery semantics after service restart specified end-to-end — pending entries resume, but do previously-published unexpired signals interact with the §FR-010 re-emission rule when in-memory last-decision state is lost? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-010] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: after restart the strategy re-warms (FR-013, FR-024), so its first post-warm-up decision may duplicate a still-unexpired prior signal — covered by SBC-002's duplicate-tolerance clause (at-least-once).
- [x] CHK031 Is "input stall" (§FR-014, §FR-020) distinguished from "empty market" (no events because nothing is happening) with distinct detection criteria and alert severities? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014, §FR-020] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-014 now distinguishes per-asset staleness (suppression + one-time LOW alert) from stream-level input stall (zero entries for the threshold — MEDIUM alert).
- [x] CHK032 Are health-alert severities assigned per failure class (crash vs restart vs permanent failure vs stall vs validation failure), or is severity left undefined for all but permanent failure? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020, §US3] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-020 now maps the shared `Severity` enum — restart MEDIUM, permanent failure HIGH, stall MEDIUM, validation failure LOW, Redis disconnect HIGH.
- [x] CHK033 Is SC-004's "5 seconds to health alert" achievable-by-requirement — is any alerting latency requirement present in the FRs, or does SC-004 measure something no FR mandates? [Traceability, Spec §SC-004, §FR-020] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-020 mandates the alert mechanism; SC-004 is its quantified acceptance bound. FR + SC together form the requirement, consistent with how SCs complement FRs across the spec.

## Contracts & Integration

- [x] CHK034 Is the `Signal` schema fully specified for contract purposes — field types, optionality, serialization form on the stream (envelope payload shape), and `schema_version` handling within the `MarketEvent` envelope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, §FR-009, §SBC-002] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: the spec-level contract (fields, constraints, envelope wrapping) is complete in FR-007/FR-009; serialization form, optionality, and schema_version detail are data-model.md/contracts artifacts, explicitly assigned by SBC-005.
- [x] CHK035 Is the envelope mapping defined without conflict — `MarketEvent.asset` vs `Signal.asset`, envelope `timestamp` vs signal `timestamp`, and does `source="nexus-strategies:{strategy_name}"` satisfy the envelope's source conventions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, CLAUDE.md envelope rules] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-009 now pins the mapping — envelope `asset` = `Signal.asset`, envelope `timestamp` = `Signal.timestamp`, payload = serialized Signal.
- [x] CHK036 Does the spec state whether `Signal.asset` may itself be a `sector:` tag or `None`, or must always be a concrete tradable pair — and is that consistent with the aggregator's expected input? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-016] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-007 now requires `Signal.asset` to be a concrete tradable pair (never `sector:`/`None`); sector and general-market sentiment are inputs, not signal targets.
- [x] CHK037 Are ordering guarantees for `nexus:signal-events` specified (per-strategy order, per-asset order, none), given the aggregator will time-window and weight contributing signals? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, §SBC-002] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-009 now guarantees per-strategy, per-asset emission order; nothing across strategies.
- [x] CHK038 Is stream retention/trimming (MAXLEN) for `nexus:signal-events` specified or explicitly deferred, so the aggregator's replay expectations are bounded? [Gap, Spec §FR-009] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-009 sets approximate MAXLEN 50,000 (= sentiment `output_maxlen`); FR-020 sets 5,000 for the health stream (platform convention).
- [x] CHK039 Are consumer-group naming and ownership specified for the two input streams (group names, one group per service vs per strategy), consistent with the Assumption that groups are engine-owned? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, §Assumptions] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: FR-001 now names `nexus-strategies-group` (per-stream scoped, `nexus-<service>-group` convention), consumer `consumer-{instance}`, 5000 ms block timeout — matching nexus-sentiment.
- [x] CHK040 Is the impact on `nexus:market-events` producers validated — the stream currently has no consumer groups; is the assumption that XREADGROUP-based consumption requires no upstream change (e.g., retention/trim policy) documented and correct? [Assumption, Dependency, Spec §SBC-003] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: SBC-003 documents it, and it is technically correct — consumer groups are created consumer-side (`XGROUP CREATE ... $ MKSTREAM`, FR-001) with no producer-side change.
- [x] CHK041 Is the sector-tag subscription contract precise — the Assumptions say strategies declare sector tags in config with no global mapping, but §US4's independent test says sector scores reach "strategies whose configured assets belong to that sector mapping"; do these agree? [Conflict, Spec §US4, §FR-016, §Assumptions] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: verified §US4 already reads "subscribed to that sector tag" (the conflicting wording existed only in a discarded draft); FR-016 strengthened with an explicit "engine MUST NOT derive sector membership from asset lists" clause.
- [x] CHK042 Are requirements defined for `SentimentScore` fields the strategy actually receives (score, confidence, label, model_id passthrough) — is the strategy-facing input type a defined contract or left to the plan? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-002, §FR-016] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: strategy-facing inputs are the existing `nexus-common` `MarketEvent`/`SentimentScore` contracts (SBC-001 dependency, defined in 002); no new input type is introduced at spec level.
- [x] CHK043 Is backward/forward compatibility specified for consuming events with unknown `schema_version` or unknown `event_type` values on input streams? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-001, §FR-015] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: unknown `event_type` or incompatible `schema_version` fails `MarketEvent` schema validation and takes the FR-015 ack/log/drop path; no strategy is invoked with an unrecognized event.
- [x] CHK044 Are the `nexus-common` additions (Signal, `SIGNAL` enum value) covered by contract-snapshot (syrupy) test expectations in the spec's success criteria, matching the repo's established contract-test layout? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §SBC-002, §SC-005] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: contract-snapshot coverage is the repo-wide `tests/contract` convention (CLAUDE.md test layout), enforced at the tasks phase; consistent with 002, whose spec likewise did not restate it in success criteria.
- [x] CHK045 Does every SBC item map to a concrete downstream artifact obligation (data-model.md entry, contracts/ file, future-spec reference), and is SBC-005's list complete against §FR-009/§FR-012? [Traceability, Spec §SBC-005] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: SBC-005 names data-model.md/contracts for the Signal + `SIGNAL` additions and future-spec references for the FR-009 stream and FR-012 seams — complete against both FRs.

## Cross-Cutting Consistency & Measurability

- [x] CHK046 Do SC-001 (1-second signal latency) and SC-002 (10 strategies × 20 assets) state their measurement conditions (event rate, hardware class, steady-state definition) well enough to be objectively verified? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: SC-001 now defines steady state (post-warm-up, no backlog) and the hardware class; SC-002 pins the rate at ≥1 event/sec/asset.
- [x] CHK047 Is terminology used consistently across the spec — "decision horizon" vs "timeframe" vs "candle interval", "engine" vs "Strategy Manager", "stale" vs "stalled" — with each term having a single definition? [Consistency, Spec throughout] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: "decision horizon" is defined in Key Entities (timeframe/candle interval used only as its explanation), Strategy Manager is defined as the engine's supervising component, and "stale" (data) vs "stalled" (input feed) are used distinctly in FR-014.
- [x] CHK048 Are all Assumptions either validated, converted to requirements, or flagged for `/speckit.clarify` — in particular the deferred process-per-strategy decision, the no-TimescaleDB-persistence choice, and the expiry-equals-one-horizon default? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] — **Resolved 2026-07-15**: all three carry explicit dispositions in Assumptions — process model deferred to the plan phase, signal persistence delegated to downstream audit trail, expiry default config-overridable.

- Gate complete 2026-07-15: **48/48 resolved** — 19 verified as already answered by the spec; 29 resolved via spec amendments (FR-001, FR-005, FR-007–FR-011, FR-014, FR-016, FR-017, FR-020, FR-022, new FR-024/FR-025, SBC-002, Assumptions, SC-001–SC-003, SC-008, edge cases). All defaults trace to existing nexus-ingestion/nexus-sentiment values except the 500-char reasoning bound and 1-hour expiry cap, which had no precedent. Spec is ready for `/speckit.plan`.
